title: gateway: guarantee request-id + retry-after response headers (and expose for browser clients)
author: Amara Diallo
description:
Context: As part of the SDK parity audit (auth/retries/timeouts/streaming), we need gateway responses to be consistent and machine-parseable for client-side retry logic and support debugging. Today, request IDs are not guaranteed on all codepaths (notably some early rejects) and Retry-After is inconsistently populated on throttling/overload responses.

What this PR does: (1) Guarantees a stable request identifier header on every response, including 4xx produced before upstream dispatch. (2) Standardizes Retry-After semantics for 429 and selected 503 responses where we expect clients to back off. (3) Updates gateway tests to lock the behavior.

Changes:
- Always attach `request-id` response header.
  - If an upstream service provides an ID, we pass it through (normalized).
  - Otherwise the gateway generates one at the edge (UUIDv4) and uses the same value for structured logs.
  - Header is present for success, errors, and early rejections (auth missing, payload too large, etc.).
- Standardize `retry-after` on throttling/overload responses.
  - For HTTP 429: always set `retry-after` (seconds) derived from limiter state.
  - For HTTP 503 due to capacity/overload (explicit gateway overload path): set `retry-after` (seconds) using a conservative backoff value.
  - For other 5xx: do not set `retry-after` (avoid implying safe retry timing when not known).
- Browser friendliness:
  - Ensure CORS exposes `request-id` and `retry-after` so JS SDKs can read them (`access-control-expose-headers` append).
- Tests:
  - Added/updated gateway integration tests to assert headers on: 200, 401 (missing key), 429 (rate limit), 503 (overload), and 500 (no retry-after).
  - Added regression test for “early reject” path to ensure request-id is still emitted.

Why: SDKs (python/ts/go) are converging on shared retry budgets and backoff guidance. `request-id` is required for customer support correlation and to safely dedupe retry storms in telemetry. `retry-after` reduces guesswork and prevents aggressive client retry loops (ref: SUP-9334).

Notes / non-goals:
- This PR does not change server-side retry behavior (no internal retries added).
- This PR does not change rate limit policy or quotas; only the response contract.

Checklist:
- [x] Gateway emits request-id on all responses
- [x] retry-after semantics documented in code comments and tested
- [x] CORS expose headers updated
- [x] SRE + Security review for log safety (no sensitive data added)

Follow-ups:
- Docs/SDK work will reference this contract (ENG-2490). Separate PR will align the 429 error payload fields (see pr-18343 / PM comms).
commits: gateway: always set request-id header (generate if missing)
gateway: expose request-id + retry-after via CORS
tests(gateway): assert request-id present on early rejects
tests(gateway): add retry-after assertions for 429/503 paths
chore: tighten header normalization + add helpers
test_plan: 1) `pnpm test gateway/tests/integration/headers_request_id.test.ts` 2) `pnpm test gateway/tests/integration/headers_retry_after.test.ts` 3) Local run with `GATEWAY_OVERLOAD_MODE=1` and confirm 503 responses include `retry-after` and `request-id` 4) Verify browser fetch can read headers (CORS expose) in quick manual check.
review_conversation:
Brian Murphy: Can we confirm header naming/casing? Our SDK spec drafts refer to `request-id` (lowercase in docs), but Node fetch exposes headers case-insensitively. I mostly care about the actual key.

Amara Diallo (author): Gateway emits `request-id` and `retry-after` as canonical keys. Internally we normalize incoming variants (`x-request-id`, `x-redwood-request-id`) and always write `request-id` on the way out. Added tests asserting the canonical name.

Rafael Mendes: Please avoid setting `retry-after` on generic 5xx. Otherwise SDKs may treat unknown failures as “safe to retry later” and we’ll amplify load during incidents.

Amara Diallo (author): Agreed. Updated logic: only set `retry-after` for 429 and the explicit overload 503 path. For upstream 5xx or gateway 500, no header is set. Added a test for 500 to assert absence.

Ibrahim Khan: For parity, SDKs want `request-id` even on missing/invalid API key errors. Currently I think auth middleware rejects before request-id injection.

Amara Diallo (author): Good catch. Re-ordered middleware so request-id is assigned before auth evaluation. Added `401_missing_key_has_request_id` regression test.

Marcus Lin: Any risk of leaking secrets via request-id (e.g., derived from key) or logs? Please confirm the ID is random and not tied to auth.

Amara Diallo (author): It’s UUIDv4 generated at edge when missing; never derived from auth. Also ensured no headers are logged verbatim besides request-id. No changes to auth logging. Thanks.

Ethan Park: Looks good. One nit: retry-after should be integer seconds per RFC; ensure we’re not returning ms.

Amara Diallo (author): Fixed: limiter returns ms; now we `Math.ceil(ms/1000)` and clamp to [1, 120]. Tests updated accordingly.

Ethan Park: Approved.
release_notes:
- Gateway now guarantees `request-id` on every response (including early 4xx rejects) to support SDK debugging and support correlation.
- Gateway standardizes `retry-after` (seconds) for 429 and explicit overload 503 responses; other 5xx will not include `retry-after`.
- CORS now exposes `request-id` and `retry-after` for browser-based SDK usage.
